A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ROSITA by the same authors, despite the changed title and terminology. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison. Local reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison of the work overall.

before.justification: V1 reports original adaptation experiments, baseline comparisons, loss ablations, continual-domain evaluations, and five-seed results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original ROSITA experiments and adds benchmark comparisons, parameter studies, representation-distance measurements, and failure diagnostics.

M1.justification: Matching Equations 1–8 across versions shows the same proposed procedure: dynamic LDA identification, reliability filtering, two feature banks, pseudo-label and contrastive losses, and vision-encoder LayerNorm updates with fixed text classifiers. ReDUCe renames the existing objective, and desired/undesired replaces weak/strong OOD terminology. Alternative detectors and parameter choices are evaluated as controls rather than replacing ROSITA's procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds DomainNet Clipart, Painting, and Sketch evaluations with MNIST, plus CCC/MNIST streams with gradual corruption changes. It also extends continual evaluation to CIFAR-100C and tests rapidly changing domains. These substantially broaden domain and temporal-condition coverage. Some earlier combinations, including VisDA/SVHN, no longer have reported results.

E2.justification: V1's main comparisons use ZS-Eval, TPT, TPT-C, and the MaPLe-based PAlign variants. V2 Tables 1–3 additionally evaluate (K+1)PC, UniEnt, TDA, and DPE on retained benchmarks. Appendix C.4 also adds DAF detector comparisons and crosses detector choice with UniEnt versus ReDUCe objectives.

E3.justification: V2 expands parameter-selection experiments to additional attention blocks, combined prompt/LayerNorm updates, LoRA ranks, and SGD/AdamW controls. It replaces the appendix's ViT-B/32 and ResNet-50 evaluations with CLIP and Open-CLIP ViT-L/14 settings, adds a 300,000-sample CCC protocol, and measures feature distances. Frequent-switching sample budgets are new, although Table 5 specifies 200 where the prose says 250. Main ROSITA hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds two previously unreported pairwise loss combinations, broader parameter and LoRA sensitivity studies, detector/objective controls, feature-separation measurements, and reliable-sample accuracy diagnostics. These test component necessity and failure mechanisms more extensively. Reliability filtering and neighbor-count analyses already existed in v1; their relocation or repetition is not counted as new analysis.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix B.1/Table 8 and v2 Appendix C.1/Table 9 report the same five-random-seed study, mean-and-standard-deviation practice, and numerical entries. V2 does not introduce additional uncertainty estimation or significance testing.

E6.justification: Shared main ROSITA scores largely remain unchanged, including 84.17 HM on CLIP CIFAR-10C/MNIST. V2 adds substantial benchmark, baseline, ablation, and diagnostic results. New comparators alter rankings: on CLIP CIFAR-100C/MNIST, (K+1)PC reaches 59.72 HM versus ROSITA's retained 57.34. Conversely, v1's detailed known/unknown accuracy tables, smaller-backbone results, and several MaPLe scenario results are removed.

T1.justification: V1 provides loss definitions and intuitive explanations; v2 adds explicit gradient analysis in Section 3.1 and Appendix A, including normalized-feature assumptions and derivations of attraction and softmax-weighted repulsion. This is substantive new mathematical analysis. However, Appendix Equations 13 and 15 omit the temperature factor present in Equation 9, and the undesired-sample gradient inconsistently uses K+ instead of K.

C1.justification: V2 elevates establishing an OSTTA benchmark to an explicit contribution in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The central claims about pioneering open-set single-image VLM adaptation, ROSITA's contrastive separation, continuous LayerNorm adaptation, and efficiency remain substantially intact. The new terminology and ReDUCe name do not themselves establish new scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's clustering explanations and brief memory/FPR limitations, v2 explains initial adaptation instability, contrasts ReDUCe with UniEnt, discusses LoRA tradeoffs, and analyzes reliable-sample quality. Section 6 explicitly acknowledges MNIST's limited realism and the absence of evaluation on streams containing no undesired classes. Appendix E adds a more specific account of difficulties on ImageNet-C and semantically similar classes.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies configurations for four added baselines, including prototype handling, cache capacities, learning rates, and optimizers. Appendix C.5 specifies LoRA placement and ranks, and the dataset inventory adds DomainNet sample counts. Existing ROSITA settings remain unchanged. V2 removes v1's asset-license inventory and changes the code-access pointer from the project website to a direct repository link.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against training-free adaptation, prototype evolution, open-set entropy objectives, and LoRA, adding the corresponding TDA, DPE, UniEnt, and LoRA references alongside CCC and Open-CLIP. It develops explicit CNN-versus-VLM and ROSITA-versus-UniEnt/(K+1)PC distinctions. Several earlier general domain-adaptation and source-free-adaptation references are dropped.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Problem setup and benchmarking move ahead of the method, parameter analysis becomes a separate main section, baseline exposition moves largely into Appendix B, and the analysis is reorganized into nine research questions. Terminology changes throughout, and the appendices are substantially reordered.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different publication layout, relabels the framework diagram, expands the parameter-selection plot, and restructures comparison tables with additional rows and improvement annotations. A combined scenario table replaces detailed main-text continual results, while reliability results move from the appendix into the main text. New diagnostic tables accompany removal of detailed result tables and the MaPLe complexity plot.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens comparative validation: v1 relied mainly on zero-shot and prompt-tuning baselines, whereas v2 includes adapted open-set and efficient alternatives and directly tests detector, objective, and parameter choices. Broader domain-shift evaluations and specific failure diagnostics further clarify applicability. These address important weaknesses in the original evidence. The gains are qualified by removal of detailed known/unknown accuracy results, the 200/250-sample inconsistency, gradient-normalization errors, and superiority wording that exceeds some new results. Nevertheless, the stronger controls and comparative evidence establish a substantial overall improvement.
